title: Mara and the Debt
premise: Ivo Fairweather, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his wife and daughter in row twelve, receives a call on a burner phone from a voice he buried years ago: Mara Voss, the defector whose testimony once destroyed his career. She claims the crash that killed his family was staged to cover her extraction, and that the people who arranged it now want her dead before she can recant. As Ivo smuggles her toward a dawn flight out of a snowbound coastal airfield, he realizes she may be bait in a trap designed to flush out the last person who knows the truth — him. In the end, Ivo chooses truth over survival, exposing the conspiracy at the cost of the flight, and Mara escapes alone carrying the evidence that finally gives row twelve its answer.
about_author: Edmund Underhill is the pen name of a former aviation-industry analyst who spent a decade writing safety reports before turning to fiction. He lives on the North Sea coast, where the weather does half his plotting for him.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash, Ivo reviews a closed case file and notices an anomaly in the wreckage manifest he's seen a hundred times but never questioned. The emotional beat is grief sharpening into suspicion as a detail refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A phone wrapped in plastic appears in his mailbox; when it rings, Mara Voss — the defector who testified against him seven years ago — says his family's flight was never supposed to land. Emotional beat: disbelief curdling into rage, then a terrible, hungry hope.

chapters.title: What the Black Box Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo and Mara POVs. Ivo pulls archived telemetry while Mara, hiding in a Rotterdam safehouse, explains how her handlers faked the data. Their accounts begin to corroborate. Emotional beat: two enemies forced into reluctant alignment by shared evidence.

chapters.title: Handlers
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Her old handler, Callum Reeve, finds her safehouse; she escapes through the docks with a drive containing the original flight orders. Emotional beat: paranoia and betrayal, revealing Mara has been running from her own side longer than from Ivo's.

chapters.title: The Extraction File
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Decoding the drive, Ivo learns the dawn flight was scheduled months ago — before Mara ever called him — meaning someone predicted exactly this chain of events. Emotional beat: dread, as rescue begins to look like choreography.

chapters.title: Halden Airfield
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Ivo drives north through a storm to the airfield while Mara moves separately, both shadowed by a clean-handed man who never checks in twice. Emotional beat: grim momentum, trust tested at every checkpoint.

chapters.title: The Man Who Never Checks In Twice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She identifies their tail as Wren, the operative who ran the row-twelve operation, and realizes Ivo was chosen as escort precisely because grief makes him predictable. Emotional beat: guilt — she must decide whether to tell him he's the trap's second target.

chapters.title: Confession at the Fence Line
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the airfield perimeter, Mara confesses everything, including her role in the cover-up that killed his family. Ivo nearly walks away; instead he chooses to finish it — not for her, but for row twelve. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Dawn Flight
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. Wren springs the trap on the tarmac; Reeve turns out to be playing his own angle. Ivo broadcasts the flight orders over the airfield frequency, forcing witnesses, and wrecks the plane rather than let the operation fly. Emotional beat: sacrifice and chaos.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Resolution, Ivo's POV. Weeks later, the leaked orders reopen the crash investigation; row twelve finally gets its true cause recorded. Mara is gone, somewhere east, alive. Ivo stands at the graves with the corrected report. Emotional beat: costly peace — truth survived, loyalty did not.
